newsitem.title: POLAND: Poland's Fortuna NFI fund eyes 5 firms for float.
newsitem.headline: Poland's Fortuna NFI fund eyes 5 firms for float.

text.p: Poland's Fortuna SA National Investment Fund (NFI no 13) plans to float five leading companies out of its portfolio with one earmarked for bourse listing later this year, the fund's president said on Thursday.
"We are preparing (textile firm) ZPJ Wistil for bourse listing and it should happen probably in the third or fourth quarter of this year," Jan Waluszewski told Reuters in an interview.

He added that in 1998 further three companies: construction firm Budostal-2 SA, leather firm Lubelskie Zaklady Skorzane SA, and Warsaw-based pump producer Warszawska Fabryka Pomp SA could become listed.
Waluszewski said two construction firms in Pulawy and Radom could be merged into a bigger company ahead of a possible flotation.
He said that at the end of 1996 liquid assets acquired through sales of shares from the fund's portfolio and other operations amounted to 23 percent of Fortuna's total assets.
"In 1996 we have carried out several succesful transactions, including the sale of a stake in Nowiny cement plant and a 13-percent stake in diesel engines maker Andoria," Waluszewski said.
He said large strategic stakes of 33 percent or more accounted for 42 percent of the fund's portfolio, while small minority stakes accounted for 35 percent.
Waluszewski said the fund wanted to remain a stakeholder in its most attractive companies along with strategic investors.
"We consider bringing in investors from a given industry who would work alongside the fund," he said.
Under Poland's mass privatisation programme, 15 NFIs were given control of stakes of over 60 percent in more than 500 medium-size companies.
Each fund, run by international managers, was given a leading, 33 percent stake in more than 30 companies and small equity stakes in the remaining firms.
From May 12, the 26 million Poles who bought participation units in the scheme have been entitled to exchange them for 15 shares, one in each fund, which start trade on the Warsaw bourse on June 12.
